— the walk to the buffet: give herself somewhere to be going, so standing still doesn't read as waiting; keep her chin level while she counts the couples she passes.
— setting the clutch down: give her hands a job and herself a reason to be standing there, then turn back to the room and keep looking anyway, because she is not ready to stop.

PHYSICS
The rifle has real mass: held up it wanders and trembles, and when the muzzle sinks it swings with weight; he keeps two hands on it long after it has stopped being useful. Getting him up is a genuine two-person struggle — she braces, her knees bend, her shoulder goes under his arm, he pushes off the ground with one hand, wet litter slides under his palm, his boots skid once before finding purchase, and afterwards his weight visibly pulls her sideways and shortens her stride. Wet corduroy and canvas hang heavy and dark with water. The wolf print is pressed real into saturated mud with raised rims, collapsed edges and standing water, leaves stuck around it. The pendant lifts with a slight suction release, mud clinging in the etched grooves and to the snapped cord, and it swings once on the cord before her fist closes. The dead torch lies where it fell and never moves. Leaf litter stays churned and dark where the fight was. Woodsmoke keeps rising from the chimney. No breath vapour despite the cold.

LIGHTING
Near-black woodland dusk. There is NO artificial light anywhere in this scene: the cottage windows stay dark and unlit, there is no porch lamp, no moon, and the fallen torch is dead — its lens is black, it lights nothing, and it is never switched on. Every bit of illumination is the last flat sky light coming down through the gaps between bare branches: weak, cool, directionless blue-green, arriving from above and slightly behind, so the tops of shoulders, cheekbones, wet hair and the rims of the mud puddles carry a faint sheen while everything underneath falls away into darkness. Faces are modelled by that top light only and read low-key and half-lost. The pale sky gaps between the trunks are the brightest thing in frame and both figures silhouette softly against them. On the ground insert, the same weak sky light gives a soft top sheen to wet mud and the pendant takes one small cold specular on its cleanest facet — that glint is the only bright point in the shot and it is what her eye catches.
The flash insert is lit in complete opposition to everything around it: bright flat neutral daylight, warm-neutral white balance, clean and soft. The cut from black woodland dusk into that daylight is itself the shock.
EXPOSURE: the whole scene sits about two-thirds of a stop under normal exposure — a very dark, cinematic, low-key image matching the attack exactly. Shadows are deep but never crushed to flat pure black; the mud, the print, the wet fabric and the trunks keep detail inside the darkness. Both faces stay readable and the pendant stays clearly legible in the insert. No lifted flat video look, no digital brightening, no bright even ambient fill, no moonbeam, no daylight leaking into the dusk scene, no light source that is not the sky.

Wind high in bare branches, dripping trees, the wet suck of mud and leaves, his ragged winded breathing, the wooden knock of the rifle stock, her running footsteps arriving on loose gravel then on leaf litter, the small wet release as the pendant comes out of the mud, then two sets of uneven footsteps moving away up the concrete path and up wooden steps.

The wind and the woods drop away with it. Only her own breathing and the small close sounds of the pendant in her fingers stay present and sharp. At the last beat the world comes back to normal level in one clean step as she closes her fist. No musical sting, no reverb wash, no ringing tone, no heartbeat effect — the effect is made only with level, distance and muffling.

SCENE CONTEXT
Cold blue-grey dusk, deep woods. <<<image_1>>> is walking home alone along the dirt track from school — tired, ordinary, nothing wrong. A single rifle shot cracks through the trees somewhere ahead of her. She runs. She comes onto the ground in front of her father's dark cottage and finds <<<image_3>>> standing crooked with the rifle up, aiming into the black trees. She runs to him; his leg gives out and she catches him and takes his weight. She asks what happened; he tells her two wolves. He keeps muttering about the wolves — and while he mutters, her eyes drop to the ground and find a small silver pendant lying in the mud beside a wolf print. From that moment his voice goes far away and muffled, as though heard through water. She picks the pendant up. She has seen it before — today, hanging at a boy's collar. She puts it in her pocket while her father is still talking to the trees, and then takes his weight again and helps him inside. British accents.

ACTING TASK — JADE (the work happens in her eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (unspoken): walk in as if she belongs here.
MOTIVE: the dress is her mother's; wearing it in is a promise she is keeping to two people at 
once.
GOAL: get to those stairs and up them without letting anyone see what this costs her.
OBSTACLE: she does not believe she belongs, every step across this floor is an argument with 
herself — and then he steps into her path and names the thing she is most afraid of.
TACTIC: keep her eyes on her own route, get to the rail, and when he blocks it, hand the cut 
straight back wrapped in manners and take her exit through him rather than around him.
— crossing the floor: her eyes are working the distance to the stairs, breaking it into 
stages, checking the nearest people only for whether they have noticed her. Her hands keep 
finding the clutch and the skirt for something to hold. The near-stop is her nerve going and 
being overruled.
— he lands in front of her: a beat of pure recalibration — someone is in the way, and only 
then, who it is.
— his line: her eyes check both of his — is he laughing at me, or is this simply how he 
speaks — and she cannot tell, which is worse.
— her line: she gives him the politest possible words and empties them of everything, 
watching his face for whether the flatness lands.
— the shoulder: not temper, punctuation. He is standing in her way and she removes the 
problem, no harder than she has to.

MOTIVE: she interests him precisely because she does not want to be here.
GOAL: get a real reaction out of her — anything that isn't the polite mask.

he rather admires both.
TACTIC: come down to her, put himself in her way, arrive with a flourish, show off his own 
finery so the comparison does the cutting for him, and read her face for the flinch.
— coming down the stairs: he spots her from above and picks his moment, adjusting his pace so 
he lands in front of her rather than beside her.
— the turn: performed for no one in particular and for everyone — this is simply how he 
occupies a room, and he neither checks whether anyone is watching nor cares.

finery on display so that hers has to be measured against it, and watches her eyes to see 
whether she makes the measurement.

curiosity. She was better than he expected.

his fun and has no intention of apologising for it.
